Reconstruction and drift check
I rebuilt the working tree from dump.txt with SHA-256 verified per file: 382 of 382 byte-exact. The two that never verify are the two that never verify — export.sh, whose dump rewrites its own header into the copy it embeds, and LICENSE, which the exporter elides to metadata by design. One file needed trimming before it hashed: RestaurantTimeTests.cs is last in the dump and swallows the DUMP SUMMARY footer; trimmed, it matched 7575227f6bf4… exactly.

Carried session memory said Slice 60, v1.45, 1281 tests, floor 33, F-113. The tree says Slice 64, v1.49, 1302 tests, floor 37, F-118 — drift of four slices, caught by the ritual for the seventh time. Nothing was authored before that was settled. Per your own standing rule, the baseline at Slice 64 was a measurement (1302 passed / 0 failed / 0 skipped), and Slice 64 predicted 1302 unchanged.

What the next slice is
The menu plan's own closing register names it, in as many words: "Nothing measures §11.1 with a picture on a card … It is the cheapest remaining thing in this file." That is Stage 1e, and its recorded blocker is precise — attaching a photograph inside scenario 21 means extracting the upload journey into the harness.

I confirmed the blocker is real and the shape of the work:

The upload journey exists only inline inside MenuPictureScenarios, with #picture-file, #picture-status, .status-success and img.manage-picture-image as private const. A second scenario file cannot reach any of it — F-100's situation exactly, one register over from TableJourneys.SeatGuestAsync in Slice 64.
PictureFixtures.SquareGradientPng(edge) already generates a real PNG of a chosen size, so no fixture work is needed. At edge 400 the file is 480,503 bytes against §8.2's cap of 524,288 — inside it, so menu-picture.js reports "stored exactly as it is" and the server stores a 400×400 PNG verbatim. No JPEG re-encode, no ladder, nothing non-deterministic.
Why 400 and not 12. .order-menu-detail-picture carries max-width: 100%; height: auto, and that stylesheet's own comment says why: "a 3000px photograph would make the DOCUMENT wider than a 375px viewport". A 12px fixture renders 12px and proves the declaration does nothing. A 400px intrinsic image inside a ~300px panel is the arrangement in which that declaration is load-bearing — remove it and ScrollsSideways fails.

And the vacuity trap I found on the way in, which is F-41's shape. An <img> that has not decoded has zero intrinsic size, so its box is 0×0 — and a 0×0 box trivially lies inside the viewport. Worse, the required-selector census would report img.order-menu-detail-picture × 1, matched, so Slice 64's own refusal cannot see it. The barrier would pass while measuring a placeholder. The card's thumbnail is loading="eager" only for heading index 0, which is where scenario 21's items sit — true today, and not a contract.

That makes two things load-bearing rather than tidy: a decode wait in the harness before measuring, and a collapsed-box refusal in the barrier scoped to a new selector group for elements sized by their own bytes rather than by padding and text.

What is finished and verified
Reconstruction. The tree survived from the previous turn, so no re-verification was needed. State confirmed: Slice 64, v1.49, 1302 measured, floor 37, F-118.

The four code files are written.

tests/MyRestaurant.EndToEnd.Tests/Harness/MenuPictureJourneys.cs — new. AttachAsync, WaitForDecodedAsync, SettleAsync, and the six selectors as internal const. The two JS predicates compose their selectors from those constants rather than quoting them, because a script is where a second spelling hides best.
HandheldReach.cs — fourth group ReachOnlySelectors, MeasuredControl gains Width, the collapsed-box refusal, AllSelectors(surface) extracted so the census and the refusal cannot walk different sets, script returns width and groups[3].
MenuReactionScenarios.cs — steps (n) and (o), WideFixtureEdge = 400.
MenuPictureScenarios.cs — six literals now point at the harness constants, and WaitForResizeReportAsync defers to SettleAsync instead of carrying a duplicate of the five-line script.
Byte hygiene and the standing authoring scans, emulated over all four: braces, parens and brackets balanced; no CR; exactly one final newline; no trailing whitespace; no whitespace-only line; every string.Create operand an interpolated literal; no await in an interpolation hole.

Sensitivity proof: fourteen planted defects, all caught by the intended verdict. The new decision logic was transcribed out of C# into Python — written from it, not read by it — and driven against synthesised reports. Two results are worth your attention:

A 20px-tall thumbnail reports GREEN, and that is the design. It confirms the reach-only group genuinely withholds the touch-target verdict rather than accidentally inheriting it.
Two cases isolate the reach half of the new group — a panel picture off the edge with the document not scrolling, and a thumbnail off the edge. Both report OutOfReach, so the group's own reach check is live and is not being carried by the ScrollsSideways assertion sitting above it.
The rest: baseline green; an undecoded panel picture and an undecoded thumbnail each refused as collapsed; a silent upload refused by name; max-width: 100% deleted; a card pushed off the edge; the 15px basket box; a 34px like control; a renamed .order-menu-inspect; a reader returning nothing.

The fixture arithmetic checks out. SquareGradientPng(400) is 480,503 bytes against §8.2's 524,288 cap — about 43 KB of headroom, so menu-picture.js takes the file.size <= budget branch, says "stored exactly as it is", and the server stores a 400×400 PNG verbatim. 420 would be 529,728 and over. Both properties of that number are load-bearing and neither is a copy of the cap.

What remains
TECHNICAL_SPECIFICATION.md has its header at v1.50, the §16.4 reach-only paragraph, the §16.3 scenario 21 extension, and the four-groups correction. Still outstanding: the Appendix A row, the changelog entry, and then MENU_AND_HANDHELD_PLAN.md (Stage 1e), DOCUMENTATION_REVIEW.md, BUILD_PROGRESS.md, _CHANGES.md — plus the gate emulations that have to run after the documents are final: the §16.4 counted-class census, the Markdown table gate, and the version gate.

The two things to carry forward regardless
Deletions: none. One new file needs git add — tests/MyRestaurant.EndToEnd.Tests/Harness/MenuPictureJourneys.cs. Gates key on git ls-files and are blind to it until you do.

Predicted count stays 1302. Scenario 21 is extended inside its existing [Fact]; no test class is added; MinimumCountedClasses stays 37 (MenuPictureJourneys.cs is not a *Tests.cs); §16.3 stays at 21 scenarios. Any other number is the first thing to investigate.

The fixture arithmetic checks out. SquareGradientPng(400) is 480,503 bytes against §8.2's 524,288 cap — about 43 KB of headroom, so menu-picture.js takes the file.size <= budget branch, says "stored exactly as it is", and the server stores a 400×400 PNG verbatim. 420 would be 529,728 and over. Both properties of that number are load-bearing and neither is a copy of the cap.
